Alex T: Quick check — I'm seeing weird p99 regressions after the kernel-selector change when microbatch=4 vs microbatch=1. Replay and synthetic disagree.
Priya R: Which exact commands did you run? replay vs synthetic often differ in KV warmup + seqlen distribution.
Alex T: ran: `bench/run_benchmark --mode=replay --trace=prod-2026-03-02 --microbatch=4 --kv-warmup=true`
Alex T: then: `bench/run_benchmark --mode=synthetic --shape="[1,8,256]" --microbatch=4`
Jamie K: Two quick suspects: 1) kernel-selector picks different forward kernels when batch>1, 2) KV cache warmup pattern in replay produces longer tails.
Marta S: Also measurement window. Our p99 is aggregated across the full 30m run — that masks short 10s bursts. For tails we should use sliding 10s windows.
Li W: Proposed protocol: 1) replay with original client pacing (no zeroing) to see real inter-arrivals; 2) short synthetic ramp to saturate batcher; 3) emit per-worker kernel-chooser logs + per-token latency histograms.
Alex T: I only get opaque IDs in traces. Can someone share kernel-selector log format?
Jamie K: I added a log export to bench yesterday. Format: `ts,worker,model,seq_len,microbatch,chosen_kernel,lat_ns`. Example:
```
1768499001,worker-3,gptx-13b,256,4,fused_attention_v2,123400
1768499001,worker-3,gptx-13b,128,1,attention_simple,51200
```
Priya R: Good. If fused_attention_v2 is selected only for microbatch>=2 and does extra memcopy on certain seq_len combos, that could explain p99. We need per-call kernel timings, not just chosen_kernel.
bench-bot: automated-bench-link: https://bench.internal/1768501234/run/42 (raw traces + kv-access heatmaps)
Alex T: looking at the bench link — I see 2–3 ms spikes on a subset of workers aligned with kernel switch events.
Marta S: Two concrete bench changes: a) emit per-token kernel latency, b) compute sliding-window p95/p99 (10s and 1min) and expose both.
Li W: Also capture serialized KV access pattern for the first N requests so synthetic can replay the exact prefix behavior; otherwise synthetic cold-start is unrealistic.
Jamie K: For profiling, grab perf counters inside the kernel (L1/L2 misses, memcpy time). If fused kernel triggers extra memcpy for certain seq_len pairs that's likely the smoking gun.
Priya R: Note: hosted infra biases results if RPC retries are merged into request histograms. Strip retries before computing tail metrics.
Alex T: ack. Re-running with: `--emit-kernel-timings --sliding-window=10s --strip-retries --kv-dump=first100`.
Marta S: Run both microbatch=1 and microbatch=4 for parity. If diffs persist, bisect kernel-selector commits.
Jamie K: I'll add a microbench harness for fused_attention_v2 exercising corner seq_len combos to isolate memcpy costs.
Li W: Timeline? Can we get initial runs + kernel logs by EOD GMT? Traces are large; I'll coordinate storage.
Priya R: EOD is tight but doable for a smoke run. If noisy, schedule deeper runs tomorrow.
Alex T: spinning up runs now. Will post updated trace ts when finished. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident #2026-0312 noted — similar p99 bump in prod at 15:42 UTC, rollback applied. See incident thread for artifacts.
Alex T: adding incident artifacts to bench run for correlation.
Marta S: Action items: Priya add sliding-window metrics + retry stripping; Jamie add fused kernel microbench + perf counters; Alex run replay+synthetic with kernel timings + kv prefix dump; Li stash traces & coordinate storage. Reconvene after initial runs. :eyes:
